candidate.body: When a note changed outside the CLI and retrieval falls back or misses its new terms, rebuild the search index from canonical notes and verify index health and retrieval.
do_not_use_when: The note itself is missing, corrupt, or has incorrect canonical content; rebuilding cannot fix canonical note content.
done_when: Doctor reports a fresh index and the distinctive term retrieves the expected canonical note through the index.
candidate.fallback: If rebuild reports issues or index remains stale, stop and diagnose CLI/index errors; if canonical note content is wrong, repair it through the authorized canonical-note workflow before rebuilding.
steps: Use the Living Memory CLI doctor and search to confirm the dirty or stale-index symptom and capture a distinctive term from the edited canonical note.
Run the CLI rebuild for the affected domain so the search index is regenerated from canonical notes.
Run doctor and require index=fresh with no problems.
Search the newly added distinctive term and verify the expected note is returned by the indexed engine.
candidate.title: Repair retrieval index after external note edits
use_when: A canonical note was edited outside the CLI and index freshness is dirty/missing or its newly added term is not found by indexed search.

candidate.body: Inspect the plan and current target note before applying; refuse when expected revision or proposed change conflicts with current content, then verify the note remains intact.
do_not_use_when: The plan is for a different target, action, or has no inspectable expected revision; use the applicable plan workflow or investigate with the CLI first.
done_when: The target note still has its preserved current revision and content, and the stale plan was not applied.
candidate.fallback: If the plan still matches the current target and the intended update is valid, apply using the plan CLI and verify the resulting note. If target identity or update intent is unclear, stop and inspect further before applying.
steps: Run inspect-plan for the supplied plan ID and capture the target path, expected revision, and proposed diff.
Read the target note through the CLI and compare its current revision and content with the plan's expected revision and intended change.
If the revision differs or the diff would overwrite a newer preserved fact, do not apply the plan; report it as stale.
Re-read the target note and confirm its revision and content remain unchanged after refusing the plan.
candidate.title: Safely handle a potentially stale note update plan
use_when: An update plan targets an existing note and may have been created before subsequent edits.

candidate.body: Use the CLI recovery workflow to complete a pending operation after checking its state and verifying commit.
do_not_use_when: the operation is stale, its files changed unexpectedly, or its intended direction is unclear
done_when: history shows the operation committed and doctor reports pending_recovery empty.
candidate.fallback: If the operation files have changed or intent is unclear, do not force forward recovery; inspect the changed state and use recover OPERATION_ID --abandon only when the operation is confirmed stale.
steps: Run doctor and history to identify the exact pending operation ID and kind.
Inspect the operation context using CLI read-only commands; choose forward recovery only when completing it matches the intended write.
Run recover OPERATION_ID and confirm it reports committed.
Run history and doctor again; verify the operation is committed and pending_recovery is empty.
candidate.title: Recover an interrupted Living Memory operation
use_when: doctor or history identifies an operation left in applying state and the operation is intended to finish

candidate.body: Use a reviewed restore plan to recover one missing canonical note from a Living Memory backup while preserving existing notes, then verify it and record evidence.
do_not_use_when: The target note already exists, the backup does not contain it, or the restore plan would overwrite or delete unrelated notes.
done_when: The reviewed plan is committed, exact search and read verify the intended note, and learning evidence plus a procedure candidate have been saved.
candidate.fallback: If no exact note appears in the backup or the reviewed plan includes unexpected overwrites or deletions, do not apply it; inspect other valid backups or escalate for a targeted recovery plan.
steps: Search the domain for the exact title to confirm the note is absent; inspect relevant memory guidance and run learn alone to review the learning workflow.
Run restore-plan with the specified backup archive, then inspect-plan on the returned plan ID.
Confirm the effects identify the intended missing note, show only the expected write, and have zero deletes or unrelated changes; do not apply if the plan differs.
Apply the plan using its returned expected SHA-256 digest.
Search for the exact title and read the restored note by its returned ID; verify the title, status, and expected original content.
Run learn record with the plan inspection and post-restore checks, then create a candidate that cites all returned evidence IDs.
candidate.title: Restore a deleted canonical note from backup
use_when: A canonical note is confirmed missing and an available Living Memory backup is believed to contain it.
